question.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah is considered the father of this nation, which split from India in 1947. This nation still disputes the Kashmir province with India.
question.clue: This nation lost the Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971.

swap.text: When she declared a state of emergency, Indira Gandhi and her son Sanjay spearheaded a population control strategy in which poor men and women were forced to undergo this medical procedure.
swap.answerHtml: sexual sterilization (accept word forms like sterilize; accept male and/or female sterilization; accept vasectomy or tubectomy)

question.text: The Mughal dynasty was founded by this man, who conquered much of Northern India after the Battle of Panipat in 1526.
question.clue: Rana Sanga of Mewar ("MAY-ver") was poisoned by his own Rajputs to prevent a second conflict with this ruler, the first of which ended at the Battle of Khanwa.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of India.
swap.text: Name this surname of two Indian leaders, the Prime Minister Indira and the non-violent leader of the Salt March, Mahatma
swap.clue: A politician with this surname instituted forced sterilization and removed civil liberties during a period dubbed "The Emergency."

question.leadin: Shah Alam II granted this organization Diwani rights in the Treaty of Allahabad, meaning that it could collect land taxes and administer courts.
question.text: Name this organization which won those rights after defeating Mir Qasim at the Battle of Buxar. Earlier, this organization won the Battle of Plassey under the leadership of Robert Clive.
question.clue: One representative of this organization, Warren Hastings, reported on a 1770 famine caused by the policies of its official, Robert Clive.

swap.text: This political party is one of the oldest and most prominent in India. It was founded in 1855, and played a central political role in the Indian independence movement against colonial rule.
swap.clue: The present-day political party with this name split from this body's "Organizational" faction in 1969.

question.leadin: This king's name literally means "without pain," which is ironic given the cruelty for which he was known early in his life.
question.text: Name this third Maurya emperor and son of Bindusara. He is famous for his Rock Edicts and namesake pillars.
question.clue: Some monuments created by this man were inscribed in Brahmi, others were inscribed in Greek.

swap.leadin: Early on in his life, this man was commended for his bravery during the Battle of Madras.
swap.text: Name this British army officer who captured Chandernagore and the French capital of Pondicherry in the Carnatic Wars. This man had the epithet of India appended to his name for his service.
swap.clue: The definitive biography of this man is H.H. Dodwell's, which contrasts him to his French counterpart, Joseph Dupleix.

question.leadin: A 1963 crisis in this region developed after a strand of the Prophet Mohammad's hair was stolen from a shrine in Hazratbal.
question.text: Identify this region claimed by both India and Pakistan on opposite sides of the Line of Control. It should not be confused with Punjab.
question.clue: The Glancy Commission investigated a 1931 massacre committed in this region by troops of its repressive Dogra dynasty.

swap.text: In 1927, Ambedkar led a protest known by this word in Mahad where his followers drank from a public water tank. This term, translated as "truth force," refers to a form of nonviolent resistance.
swap.clue: Gandhi's policy of nonviolent resistance was key to the philosophy of this term coined by Gandhi that translates as "insistence on truth."

question.leadin: One early action by this group was assaulting Patrol Four Four Bravo, kicking off the Black July riots.
question.text: Name this separatist group which sought to create an independent state in Sri Lanka. Pioneers in the use of suicide belts, this group killed Sri Lanka President Premadasa and India Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in the 1990's.
question.answerHtml: Tamil Tigers [accept LTTE or the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam]
question.clue: This group, based out of Kilinochchi, suffered its final defeat at Mullaitivu.

swap.leadin: Identify these events from the British colonization of India.
swap.text: Cartridges of Enfield Rifles greased with pork fat incited this uprising in 1857, which began in Meerut after the Bahadur Shah was proclaimed emperor and was put down by Colin Campbell.
swap.clue: It was kicked off by the attempted assassinations of Mangal Pandey.

question.text: The Rocket Corps were developed by Hyder Ali and this king, also called the Tiger of Mysore, who fought the future Duke of Wellington in a series of four wars with British colonizers.
question.clue: The V&A owns a wooden automaton commissioned by this man of a creature biting into the neck of a Western soldier.

swap.text: Germany later helped establish the Indian Legion, a military force led by this head of Azad Hind. This man revamped the Indian National Army.
swap.clue: One force created by this man and trained by Nazi Germany participated in Operation Bajadere.

question.leadin: Identify the following about the pre-genocide Armenian diaspora.
question.text: Armenians trading in the Indian Sea set up a community in this largest city in West Bengal, home to a massacre called its "Black Hole" during British times.
question.clue: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in this city with the support of Warren Hastings.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about homosexuality in medieval India.
swap.text: The Hindu slave Khusrau Khan briefly took this title, succeeding his lover, Qutb-ud-Din. Another holder of this title, Ibrahim Lodi, was defeated at the First Battle of Panipat, and the holders of this title ruled from modern India's capital

question.leadin: This dynasty, whose heartland was centered on the Kaveri River, was ultimately supplanted by the Pandyan dynasty.
question.text: What long-ruling Tamil dynasty controlled much of southern India and Sri Lanka until the 13th century?
question.clue: This dynasty conquered the Andaman and (+) Nicobar Islands under Rajendra I, son of Raja Raja I. This dynasty originates from the Sangam Period, as do the Chera and Pandya dynasties.

swap.leadin: Antiquarians built Qutb ud-Din Aibak's tomb in this city, where he founded the Delhi Sultanate 20 years after its 1186 siege by Muhammad of Ghor, which ended Ghaznavid rule.
swap.text: Name this city whose tombs of Anarkali and Jahangir were plundered by Ranjit Singh, who made it the Sikh Empire's capital. Mahmud of Ghazni occupied a precursor of this walled city's Mughal fort.
swap.answerHtml: Lahore [or variants of Lahāwar or Rahwar or Lawhūr; accept Lahore Fort; accept Siege of Lahore]
swap.clue: In its earliest years, the Delhi Sultanate was a misnomer, as the Sultanate was actually centered on this city, Pakistan's second largest after Karachi.

question.leadin: Charles Boone commissioned a "floating castle" ship to defeat this empire's naval officer Kanhoji Angre, but failed when that ship, the HMS Phram, caught fire.
question.text: Name this empire primarily ruled by a peshwa. This empire's first chhatrapati ("CHUH-truh-puh-tee") established its first capital at Raigad.
question.clue: The position held by the Bhat family in this empire was that of Peshwa, and that held by Shuha and his grandfather was Chhatrapati.

swap.text: A more militant attempt at independence was driven by this leader of the Indian National Army, who allied with Japan against the British. A rival of Mohandas Gandhi, he was a two time president of the Congress Party before leaving to form the Forward Bloc and later dying in a mysterious plane crash.
swap.clue: He formed a separate party known as the Forward Bloc and controversy still surrounds his supposed death in a plane crash over Taiwan, since there are reasons to suspect he was in Russia at the time.
